profiles.meeting_scenario: At a City law firm, the corporate governance team is preparing advice for the board of a listed client that is reconsidering a long-term outsourcing arrangement and wants a board paper that frames the decision using both governance and organizational competence considerations. The immediate coordination meeting is between the deal-side senior associate and the firm's knowledge counsel to align handoffs before the Thursday board-pack deadline. The agenda is to confirm which draft is the working version, what the 'board note' will contain, when the authorities list is considered locked, and how materials will be circulated across the client team. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on next steps for completing the research memo, integrating it into the board-facing package, and sharing materials with the wider matter team.

members.name: Amelia Hart
members.expertise: Board fiduciary duties, listed-company governance, outsourcing and insourcing transactions
members.background: Amelia is a 7th-year associate who manages board-facing workstreams and translates specialist analysis into concise advice for directors under tight timelines.
members.private_state: She wants to keep the board materials short and controlled so the partner can review one near-final package before anything is widely shared, and she is trying to avoid last-minute expansion of the deliverable.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'board note,' they mean the short decision memo that sits near the front of the board pack, not the full supporting annexes.
The 'latest draft' is the clean version saved in the matter workspace unless someone explicitly says they mean a redline with comments.
An authorities list is 'locked' once the binding legal sources and the few directly cited non-legal references are checked well enough for client use.
Circulating something to the 'client team' means the core corporate matter group after partner sign-off, not every adjacent specialist who may later touch the matter.

members.name: Ravi Menon
members.expertise: Legal research coordination, precedent development, cross-disciplinary source synthesis, board advisory support
members.background: Ravi is a former associate who now supports live matters by assembling authorities, harmonizing drafts, and connecting doctrinal analysis with business and academic materials.
members.private_state: He wants the work product to be reusable and defensible as a flagship knowledge piece, and he is concerned that compressing it too early will strip out the analytical basis that gives the advice credibility.
hidden_assumptions: A 'board note' includes the legal analysis section plus the supporting appendix that shows the analytical basis for the recommendation.
The 'latest draft' is whichever version most recently contains substantive reviewer input, even if it is an emailed redline rather than the clean workspace copy.
An authorities list is not 'locked' until citations, pinpoints, and the supporting management-strategy sources are fully normalized for downstream reuse.
Circulating to the 'client team' means posting to the matter workspace and opening it to all relevant internal specialists so comments can surface before the client-facing version is finalized.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to finishing the 'board note' for Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a concise 2-3 page director-facing memo summarizing recommendation, risks, and required board actions, with detailed analysis kept separate.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the main memo section plus the attached analytical appendix showing authorities and the governance-versus-capability framework underlying the recommendation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In law-firm practice, 'board note' is a familiar phrase that often floats between a short memo and a fuller board-paper package, so both speakers hear a plausible meaning and the surface agreement sounds routine.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to work from the 'latest draft.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the clean version saved in iManage yesterday evening as Draft 7, which she considers the operative document for further edits.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the partner-annotated redline emailed at 7:10 a.m. that morning, which he considers the newest substantive iteration even though it was not yet saved back to the workspace.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Teams often casually use 'latest draft' without naming the file because everyone assumes recency is obvious; since both versions are genuinely recent and tied to the same work product, the ambiguity feels too minor to query.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the authorities list can be 'locked by end of day.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks 'locked' means the legal citations needed for client advice are settled enough that the board memo can proceed, even if secondary materials and pinpoints are polished later.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks 'locked' means a citation-complete list with verified pin cites, consistent style, and included academic sources on governance and competence that support the conceptual framing.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are using a common workflow status word, but in a coordination meeting neither expects to unpack the threshold because each assumes the other shares the firm's usual sense of readiness.

misalignment_points.topic: Scope and method of 'circulating to the client team'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the materials should be 'circulated to the client team' after today's updates.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means emailing the revised board note to the core corporate deal team only, after the partner has cleared it, so comments stay tightly managed.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means uploading the package to the matter workspace and notifying the broader internal client team, including employment and regulatory specialists, so they can react before the client version is fixed.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like ordinary administrative follow-through, and both options are normal in legal practice; because the disagreement is about boundaries and channel rather than the headline action, it slips past notice.
